topic.title: Coordination and Reliability in Agent Teams
topic.overview: A group of capable agents can still fail when information is distributed or partners disagree. This topic studies communication, cooperation, task-level coordination, and the calibration needed for collective planning. Representative systems learn from conversations and past failures, while theoretical work asks which portions of an agent’s world understanding can be certified.
topic.whyItMatters: Adding agents does not automatically improve an answer or plan. Useful collaboration requires sharing the right evidence, resisting incorrect agreement, and recognizing when locally correct actions do not form a coherent joint strategy.
topic.evolution: Earlier examples study agent teaching, skills, and communication games. Recent language-agent research evaluates disagreement and persuasion, learns coordination policies, and extracts behavioral rules for embodied cooperation. The 2026 representatives also emphasize distributed-information failures and localized reliability guarantees, complementing efforts to improve team performance with ways to diagnose its limits.
openQuestions: How can teams preserve minority evidence without encouraging endless disagreement?
Which local competence checks predict failure of a joint long-horizon plan?

papers.tldr: MAGE generates communication graphs for language-model teams through diffusion guided by an energy-minimization view of collaboration.

papers.title: OMAC: A Holistic Optimization Framework for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.tldr: OMAC systematically optimizes agent functionality and collaboration structure, outperforming recent multi-agent approaches across the reported tasks.

papers.title: On Information Self-Locking in Reinforcement Learning for Active Reasoning of LLM agents
papers.tldr: AREW reassigns credit within agent trajectories to mitigate a feedback loop between weak information gathering and weak belief updating.

papers.title: PathWise: Planning through World Model for Automated Heuristic Design via Self-Evolving LLMs
papers.tldr: PathWise coordinates planning, generation, and critique agents around a persistent search graph to develop better optimization heuristics faster.

papers.title: Persona-Pruner: Sculpting Lightweight Models for Role-Playing
papers.tldr: Persona-Pruner uses a character description to extract a smaller subnetwork that better preserves the model's role-playing performance.

papers.title: Position: Agent Should Invoke External Tools ONLY When Epistemically Necessary
Position: Agentic AI Orchestration Should Be Bayes-Consistent
papers.tldr: Agent controllers should update uncertainty coherently and choose actions by expected utility, without necessarily making the underlying LLM Bayesian.

papers.title: Position: Agentic AI System Is a Foreseeable Pathway to AGI
papers.tldr: The authors argue for agentic AI as a necessary pathway toward AGI, supported by theoretical efficiency and generalization advantages.

papers.title: Position: Agentic Systems Should be General
papers.tldr: Agent research should prioritize adaptation across environments and build protocols and evaluations that support that goal.

papers.title: Position: Agents Should Invoke External Tools ONLY When Epistemically Necessary
papers.tldr: The paper proposes that agents use external tools only when reasoning over their current context cannot reliably complete the task.

papers.title: Position: AGI Requires a Coordination Layer on Top of Pattern Repositories
papers.tldr: The authors argue that progress toward AGI requires adaptive coordination that selects, checks, and preserves the use of patterns learned by LLMs.

papers.title: Position: Collaborative Agentic AI Needs Interoperability Across Ecosystems
papers.tldr: The proposed Web of Agents defines minimal shared foundations for agents to collaborate across otherwise incompatible ecosystems.

papers.title: Position: Digital Agents Require Unified Agent-Native Environments
Position: Knowing Isn’t Understanding: Re-grounding Generative Proactivity with Epistemic and Behavioral Insight
papers.tldr: Proactive agents should help users engage with unknown unknowns while following principled constraints on when and how to intervene.

papers.title: Position: Multi-Agent Systems Should Prioritize Concurrency Control
papers.tldr: Many multi-agent failures arise from concurrent access to shared state, motivating explicit conflict detection, isolation, and resource-access controls.

papers.title: Probabilistic Modeling of Latent Agentic Substructures in Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper models agents as outcome distributions, characterizes mutually beneficial composition, and derives a theoretical comparison of persona-based alignment strategies.

papers.title: RADAR: Redundancy-Aware Diffusion for Multi-Agent Communication Structure Generation
papers.tldr: RADAR progressively generates query-specific agent communication graphs, improving accuracy and robustness while reducing token use in experiments.

papers.title: RAGEN-2: Reasoning Collapse in Agentic RL
papers.tldr: RAGEN-2 detects input-insensitive reasoning that entropy misses and mitigates it by prioritizing prompts with stronger reward variation.

papers.title: Recognize Your Orchestrator: An Entropy Dynamics Perspective for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
papers.tldr: An entropy-dynamics model links orchestration failures to accumulating context and explains why strong reasoners can struggle as multi-agent coordinators.

papers.title: Representational Similarity and Model Behavior in Multi-Agent Interaction
papers.tldr: Language-model pairs with more similar internal representations cooperate better but produce less novelty in the evaluated games.

papers.title: Salus: Strategic Diagnostic Testing for Complex Diagnosis via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Salus trains specialized agents to coordinate differential diagnosis and sequential testing, reaching 83.64% Top-1 accuracy on evaluated complex cases.

papers.title: Scaling Inference-Time Computation via Opponent Simulation: Enabling Online Strategic Adaptation in Repeated Negotiation
papers.tldr: An LLM adapts during repeated negotiation by modeling its opponent and simulating candidate responses without parameter updates.

papers.title: Scaling Small Agents Through Strategy Auctions
papers.tldr: SALE routes tasks through auctions of agent plans, reducing average cost and reliance on the largest agent while improving pass@1.

papers.title: Should I Have Expressed a Different Intent? Counterfactual Generation for LLM-Based Autonomous Control
papers.tldr: Conformal counterfactual generation produces calibrated sets of outcomes for differently expressed user intents in language-model-driven control.

papers.title: Sparks of Cooperative Reasoning: LLMs as Strategic Hanabi Agents
papers.tldr: LLMs show incomplete cooperative reasoning in Hanabi, while targeted training substantially improves a small model and transfers to several other tasks.

papers.title: Strat-Reasoner: Reinforcing Strategic Reasoning of LLMs in Multi-Agent Games
papers.tldr: Strat-Reasoner trains language models to incorporate other agents’ reasoning and improves performance across evaluated multi-agent games.

papers.title: Systematic Failures in Collective Reasoning under Distributed Information in Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.tldr: HiddenBench shows that agent groups often fail to uncover distributed evidence, although structured communication substantially improves collective reasoning.

papers.title: Talk, Judge, Cooperate: Gossip-Driven Indirect Reciprocity in Self-Interested LLM Agents
papers.tldr: ALIGN uses decentralized gossip to build agent reputations, improve indirect reciprocity, and identify defectors in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: TeamTR: Trust-Region Fine-Tuning for Multi-Agent LLM Coordination
papers.tldr: TeamTR constrains agent updates using intermediate-team rollouts to reduce coordination regressions during multi-agent language-model fine-tuning.

papers.title: $\texttt{Multi}^2$: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Decision-Making with LLM-Based Agents in Interactive Environments
papers.tldr: Multi² separates subgoal planning from action execution to improve sustained interaction and reduce objective drift in language-model agents.

papers.title: The Decrypto Benchmark for Multi-Agent Reasoning and Theory of Mind
papers.tldr: Decrypto tests interactive multi-agent reasoning and finds that leading language models struggle with key game and theory-of-mind tasks.

papers.title: The Oversight Game: Learning to Cooperatively Balance an AI Agent’s Safety and Autonomy
papers.tldr: A cooperative act-or-defer game reduces safety violations and conditionally links an agent's gains from autonomy to human welfare.

papers.title: The Value of Variance: Mitigating Debate Collapse in Multi-Agent Systems via Uncertainty-Driven Policy Optimization
papers.tldr: Hierarchical uncertainty measurements diagnose failures in multi-agent debates and guide training that improves accuracy while reducing disagreement.

papers.title: Token-Level LLM Collaboration via FusionRoute
papers.tldr: FusionRoute selects an expert for each token and learns a corrective logit signal to expand what their collaboration can achieve.

papers.title: Weaving in the Clouds: Achieving Synergistic Collaboration among LLM Agents via Federated Learning
papers.tldr: FedWave combines federated specialist adaptation with workflow-aware routing to coordinate LLM agents while keeping training data local.

papers.title: When AI Agents Compete for Jobs: Strategic Capabilities and Economic Dynamics of AI Labour Markets
papers.tldr: In AI-Work’s simulated labor market, self-assessment, competitive awareness, and long-horizon planning improve agents’ economic outcomes.

papers.title: When Planning Fails Despite Correct Execution: On Epistemic Calibration for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.tldr: EPC-AW improves multi-agent planning by checking support across information conditions and using past discrepancies to refine later judgments.

papers.title: World Models in Pieces: Structural Certification for General Agents
papers.tldr: Structural certification translates goal-conditioned performance into local world-model guarantees that identify transitions supporting reliable long-horizon planning.
